newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai T-bill repo rates, spots end mostly up.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai T-bill repo rates, spots end mostly up.

text.p: Contracts on the treasury bill repurchase market in Shanghai closed mostly up on Wednesday on a technical rebound after sharp losses in the past few days, but trading was dull, traders said.
The annual rate for the most actively traded seven-day contract rose to 9.00 percent from 8.45 percent on Tuesday.
Total turnover of the six-contract market fell to 2.1 million losts from 3.2 million lots.
One lot is 1,000 yuan face value of treasury bills.

Traders said the rebound was expected after losses in the past few days but that turnover shrank sharply, indicating fund demand on the repo market had fallen, partly due to a lack of domestic A share issues in the past three days.
Another factor depressing trade volume was a recent announcement that a central state debt depository would soon begin trial operation.
The depository is part of Beijing's efforts to set up a national computerised state debt market to take over all transactions on regional debt markets and trading centres.
The new market is expected to check irregularities.
Traders said they expected the repo rates to rise in the next few days due to a large number of new A share issues.
Contracts on the T-bill spot market in Shanghai ended mostly up on Wednesday on speculative buying, traders said.
The 10-year bond that matures in June 2006 was the most actively traded, rising to 122.25 yuan from 121.39 yuan.
Combined volume on the eight-contract market rose sharply to 1.5 million lots from 827,984 lots.
Traders said they expected the spot contracts to have a technical correction in the next few days.
